title: Worker app-server threads start the operator's MCP servers and run the lead's Codex hooks
body:
Evidence (2026-11-08, #393 first live recording of codex-cli 0.167.0, deleted after review because it carried account data): every worker thread started the 5 MCP servers of the operator's Codex home (figma, asana, builder-vm, node_repl, krn) and ran 4 user hooks from ~/.codex/hooks.json ("KRN: loading the outco…") around each turn. The first model call of a two-line brief took 19,630 uncached input tokens (test/fixtures/codex-app-server/compact.rpc, first thread/tokenUsage/updated). A worker needs neither: the lead's hooks put lead context into a worker turn, and MCP tool schemas widen every call.
Acceptance: worker threads start no MCP server and run no user hook while keeping auth (a thread/start config override, or a worker Codex home holding only auth by reference, never a copied secret). Proof: a live run with mcpServer/startupStatus/updated, hook/started and hook/completed left out of the driver's opt-out list shows none of them, and the PR reports the first-call inputTokens of `KRN_LIVE=1 node scripts/live-worker.mjs --record` before and after.
